limitations: The rule names read() and read(byte[], int, int), but not read(byte[]) or convenience methods. Other methods may delegate to a named read at runtime; whether the detector observes that delegation is implementation-dependent.
The rule does not specify how the detector handles aliases, exceptions, implicit try-with-resources closes, subclasses, or interprocedural calls.
A read event does not establish that a byte was returned, and the rule does not require reading to end-of-stream.
The message alone does not identify the missing or unexpected event.
predicates: REQUIRES generatedMessageDigest[digest] for the constructor's digest argument.
ENSURES digestedInputStream[stream, digest] as a CrySL predicate for compliant usage; this is not an independently measured digest result.
The related MessageDigest rule declares generatedMessageDigest[this] after its Get event; its constraints and analysis are separate.
detector_semantics.claim: The rule accepts the specified event order subject to its constraints and required predicate. A finding reports that the detector did not accept an observed sequence.

documented_behavior: DigestInputStream wraps an input stream and associates it with a MessageDigest. Its reads update the digest with data actually read when digesting is on, which is the default. Finalizing the computation requires a digest method on the associated MessageDigest.
Bytes bypassed by skip are not added to the digest; bytes read again after reset are added again. setMessageDigest can change the associated digest.
The inherited FilterInputStream close closes the wrapped stream. Its read(byte[]) delegates to read(byte[], 0, byte[].length).
preconditions: For the three-argument read, the rule requires len > 0, offset >= 0, and length[data] >= offset + len.
The Java InputStream contract permits len == 0 with valid array bounds and returns zero without reading bytes; the CrySL rule is stricter.
unknowns: The sources do not establish the actual input, read results, digest algorithm, provider, or consumer for a reported finding.
The particular detector's treatment of integer overflow in offset + len has not been established.

non_security_violation_shapes: Calling on(true) on a concrete DigestInputStream still in its default-on state violates the blanket prohibition but need not affect security. If the rest of the rule is satisfied, removing the redundant call preserves the same stream and digest state.
important_note: This rule specifies a call protocol and CrySL predicates, not proof that the intended bytes were hashed, that a digest was finalized or verified, or that a security failure occurred. The rule text was supplied as a fetched source; independent retrieval was unavailable in this session.

events.condition: Observes the DigestInputStream(InputStream stream, MessageDigest digest) constructor. Separately, the digest argument must satisfy generatedMessageDigest[digest].
events.name: c1 / Con

events.condition: Observes the zero-argument read overload. It is a Read event regardless of whether the call returns a byte or end-of-stream.
events.name: r1 / Read

events.condition: Observes read(byte[] data, int offset, int len), not every overload matched by the text fragment. Observing the call is distinct from satisfying length[data] >= offset + len, offset >= 0, and len > 0.
events.name: r2 / Read

events.condition: Observes close() on the governed stream. The order accepts Close after at least one Read; observing an earlier close does not satisfy that order. Whether an implicit try-with-resources close is observed depends on the detector.
events.name: cl1 / Close

events.condition: A call to on(boolean) is forbidden for either boolean value, independently of the ordered events.
events.name: forbidden on

security_semantics.runtime_claim: Whether the computed digest protects anything depends on the bytes actually read, the digest and its use, and how any expected value is authenticated or compared.
security_semantics.detector_claim: The rule checks a prescribed usage protocol and predicates, including a blanket prohibition on on(boolean).

name: DigestInputStreamSpec
semantic_scope: For each governed DigestInputStream object, the rule describes construction with an input stream and message digest, one or more specified read events, and close, along with array-slice constraints, a required digest predicate, an ensured stream/digest predicate, and a prohibition on on(boolean). It does not identify an application purpose or particular input.
known_false_positive_shapes: A valid read(data, offset, 0) with otherwise valid bounds: Java permits the zero-length read, but the rule's len > 0 constraint rejects it.
A report caused by missing a feasible execution's implicit try-with-resources close or by inventing an infeasible path, when the actual governed trace otherwise satisfies the rule.
